name: Saint Alphonsus Liguori
history: A brilliant Neapolitan lawyer who left the courts after losing a case through his own oversight, Alphonsus became a priest, founded the Redemptorists to preach to the neglected poor of the countryside, and wrote on moral theology with a gentleness that changed how confessors treated penitents. He is a Doctor of the Church and patron of confessors.
life: Alphonsus took his doctorate in law at sixteen and practised with great success until 1723, when he lost an important case through a point he had overlooked. He took it as a sign, laid his sword before a statue of Our Lady and was ordained in 1726. Preaching in the hills above Amalfi, he found shepherds and peasants who had no one to teach them, and in 1732 at Scala he founded the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer. His Moral Theology steered between rigour and laxity and taught confessors to be fathers rather than judges. He also wrote The Glories of Mary and Visits to the Blessed Sacrament, and the Christmas carol Tu scendi dalle stelle. He was bishop of Sant’Agata dei Goti from 1762 to 1775. In old age, crippled and nearly blind, he was shut out of his own congregation through a misunderstanding, and bore it patiently. He died at Pagani in 1787.
prayerTo: Saint Alphonsus, you spent yourself for the poor and the forgotten, and taught confessors to be merciful. Pray for me when I am weighed down by scruples or discouraged by my sins, that I may trust in the mercy of the Redeemer. Help me to visit Him often in the Blessed Sacrament and to love His Mother as you did. Amen.
penance: Make a short visit to the Blessed Sacrament today, as Alphonsus urged, and if it has been a while, plan your next confession.
meditation: Alphonsus wrote that whoever prays is certainly saved, and whoever does not pray is certainly lost. Is there a set time in your day that belongs to God alone?
